card.name: Linking words in abstract humanities passages
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as 'of', 'about', 'as' or 'in' right after an abstract noun or verb, in essays on music, words, philosophy or religion. The next word is often an abstract idea like religion, myth or mystery.

modes.label: Power of ...
modes.description: The word 'of' after 'power' or 'use' before an abstract or sacred noun.
modes.example: Oliver Sacks explores how the power<< of>> music can make the brain come alive.

modes.label: Philosophical quotation lead-in
modes.description: A linking word or opening quote after a verb like 'wrote' in philosophy or theology writing.

modes.label: Religious or spiritual phrasing
modes.description: A verb or linker inside devotional or theological sentences.
modes.example: - to contemplate and<< appreciate>> the divine plan; - to join with

card.writes: It seems to push toward abstract cultural and spiritual nouns such as religion, myth, mystery and analogy.
card.plain: It fires on small linking words just before an abstract idea such as music, religion or myth is named.
